title: The Fake Yearbook
premise: Silas Fairweather, a trans coder hiding behind an anonymous account, notices her school's group chat posting predictions of events that haven't happened yet—predictions that trace back to a 'yearbook' project the school board buried a decade ago. Digging in, she finds the yearbook was an experiment cataloging students' futures, and its surviving subjects are being quietly manipulated to fulfill their entries. With help from three unlikely allies who become the family she never had, Silas must expose the board's cover-up before the final entry—the one written about her—is enforced. She burns the archive publicly, chooses love over the duty of silence, and claims a future no one predicted for her.
about_author: D. M. Zhou is a former software engineer turned novelist who writes stories about queer kids outsmarting systems designed to sort them. They live in a rainy coastal city with two cats and an unhealthy collection of abandoned group chats.

chapters.title: The Account That Knew
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Five years of careful anonymity shatter when her anonymous account starts receiving messages from a group chat she never joined—messages predicting tomorrow's fire drill, then a classmate's broken arm, which happens exactly as described. The emotional beat is dread wrapped in curiosity: for the first time, being invisible isn't keeping her safe.

chapters.title: Group Chat: Unknown Members
chapters.summary: POV Silas. She traces the chat to three students: prickly debate captain Marisol, gentle stoner Theo, and perfect-on-paper Priya, each of whom received a different fragment of the same buried file. Reluctantly, warily, they compare notes. The beat is friction becoming alliance—four loners discovering they were all recruited by something they can't name.

chapters.title: What the Board Buried
chapters.summary: POV Priya. In the archive basement, Priya finds the 2015 'yearbook': not photos, but profiles predicting every student's future, signed off by the school board. Her own mother's name is on the approval page. The emotional beat is betrayal—the horror of learning the adults you trusted voted on your life before you lived it.

chapters.title: Entry 0417
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Silas locates her own entry, written five years ago, describing—with chilling accuracy—the exact life she's been forced into: isolated, invisible, compliant. She realizes her 'choices' have been managed. The beat is vertigo and rage; the careful armor she built was the cage itself.

chapters.title: The Enforcement Pattern
chapters.summary: POV Theo. Theo maps the predictions against real events and finds students whose lives derailed to match their entries—scholarships revoked, relationships sabotaged, one expulsion that preceded a documented breakdown. The beat is grief and guilt: he realizes his own slacker persona was nudged into place, and he mourns the self he might have been.

chapters.title: Marisol's Motion
chapters.summary: POV Marisol. Marisol pushes the group to go public immediately; Silas insists they need proof first, and the argument cracks open old wounds about who gets believed and who gets punished. Underneath it, Marisol admits why she cares: her older sister was entry 0302. The beat is found family forming through conflict, not despite it.

chapters.title: The Quiet Offer
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Vice Principal Wren privately offers Silas a full scholarship and a wiped record—if she hands over the group's evidence and disappears again. It's everything she's spent five years wanting, offered by the people who built her cage. The beat is temptation at its most seductive: duty to herself versus loyalty to the family she just found.

chapters.title: Ninety-Six Hours
chapters.summary: POV Priya. The chat's predictions accelerate—now naming the date the archive will be 'disposed of.' The four race to mirror the files across servers while the board closes in, and Priya must decide whether to confront her mother or protect her. The beat is desperate momentum, love tested against blood, and the choice to fight anyway.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: POV Silas. At the board's emergency session, Silas hijacks the presentation screen and reads the entries aloud—entry by entry, name by name—while Theo streams it live and Marisol and Priya hold the doors. Wren moves to stop her, and Silas finally says her own name, out loud, on record. The climax beat: visibility chosen, at maximum cost.

chapters.title: Unwritten
chapters.summary: POV Silas, months later. The board resigns, the archive is sealed under court order, and the four friends plant a garden over the old archive room—a yearbook made of living things. Silas writes no predictions, only an open page. The resolution beat: a future that belongs to no one's plan but her own, held by the people who stayed.
